title: log3gpp: Reduce use of static arrays.
description:
Instead of statically allocating _three_ huge line buffers, combine them to a
single buffer in the dynamically allocated log3gpp_t private structure and a
much smaller buffer on the stack for probing the file type.  (The buffers
never needed to be separate; There is no risk of conflict by combining them in
this way.)  Similarly consolidate a few other static variables into the struct.

Reduces libwiretap's .bss by nearly 200 kBytes at the cost of 64 kBytes of heap
usage when the parser is active.  Also eliminates conflict for those static
buffers if we ever end up concurrently using multiple instances of this parser.

notes.body: Assuming this works out well, catapult_dct2000.c will be next :)

parse_line will always use log3gpp because you're passing it in, so the first parameter could be removed.
However, I would argue a better solution is to have a structure with just protocol_name and protocol_parameter members passed in where log3gpp is passed in here and have that structure local to the function calling parse_line.

Indeed the `linebuff` argument was superfluous now... Thanks for catching that!

But I have (I think) followed your guidance for a separate structure for the protocol name and parameters... the same structure is all that `write_stub_header` needs, too.  Let me know if I accurately captured your suggestion or if I missed the mark somehow.  Thanks!

Or did you intend that the protocol parameter struct actually be _scoped_ local to `log3gpp_read` (and `log3gpp_seek_read`) instead of being a member of `log3gpp_t`?  I think I can see code paths where doing that would change the behavior of the parser, but I don't know enough about the file format to tell whether the change would be considered problematic: A record with protocol name that's **not** `"TXT"` will set `protocol_parameters`, and then a _subsequent_ record with a protocol name of `"TXT"` will – as it stands today, and unless I'm overlooking something – not update `protocol_parameters`, so the caller will continue to use the _prior_ value of `protocol_parameters` in its next call to `write_stub_header`.  Making the parameter struct local to those calling functions would cause `write_stub_header` to instead receive an empty string for `protocol_parameters` when processing the subsequent `"TXT"` record.  I can't tell if the current behavior of reusing the old value of `protocol_parameters` is intentional, harmless, "should never happen", or a defect... or a complete misunderstanding on my behalf. :grinning:

> comparing log3gpp_read and log3gpp_seek_read ... most of the code in both functions starting with parse_line could be refactored into a single helper function

Exactly. Many other wiretap modules have the read and seek-read routines call a common routine that does most of the record reading.
